quote_zh: NMST (5.0g, 0.023mol), sodium hypochlorite (100ml, 0.149mol) and ruthenium oxide (0.5g, 0.004mol) were charged into a 250ml round bottomed flask. This mixture was heated to reflux temperature under stirring for 6-8hours, cooled to 25-30°C and filtered. The filtrate obtained was further cooled to 5-10°C and acidified to pH < 3 using concentrated hydrochloric acid (18mL, 0.17mol) to form precipitated product (NMSBA).The product obtained was filtered and dried at 50°C under reduced pressure to obtain NMSBA as light yellow solid. HPLC purity > 92%; Yield: 67%; and Melting point: 207-210°C.
arithmetic_check: Two mass/mole pairs are printed, two solution volume/mole pairs, a yield and no product mass. BOTH MASS/MOLE PAIRS CLOSE. NMST: C8H9NO4S is 215.230 g/mol (RDKit MolWt from the SMILES A1 carries for NMST, Cc1ccc(S(C)(=O)=O)cc1[N+](=O)[O-], formula confirmed C8H9NO4S), so 5.0 g is 0.023231 mol, which rounds at the printed three decimal places to the printed 0.023 mol; the implied molecular weight 5.0/0.023 = 217.4 g/mol sits inside the rounding window of 0.023 mol (0.0225 to 0.0235 mol, i.e. 212.8 to 222.2 g/mol) that 215.230 also sits in. RUTHENIUM OXIDE: read as RuO2, 133.068 g/mol (RDKit, from O=[Ru]=O), 0.5 g is 0.003757 mol, which rounds to the printed 0.004 mol; the implied 0.5/0.004 = 125.0 g/mol is the artefact of rounding 0.003757 up at three decimals and not a second molecular weight. molar_mass_inconsistent is therefore NOT raised on this record. THIS IS THE PAIR EXAMPLE 1 USED AS ITS CONTROL, and it does close, independently recomputed here. The comparison across the three Examples that print this same charge is worth stating exactly, because Example 1's record drew a wider conclusion from this pair than the numbers support: computed against 215.230 g/mol, Example 1's 61.2 g is 0.28435 mol against a printed 0.278 mol (2.2% low, implied 220.14 g/mol), this Example's 5.0 g is 0.02323 mol against a printed 0.023 mol (1.0% low, implied 217.39 g/mol, inside the rounding window), and Example 3's 20 g at line 285 is 0.09292 mol against a printed 0.088 mol (5.3% low, implied 227.27 g/mol). So this Example is the only one of the three whose pair closes, and the printed mole figure is low in all three. Example 1's note that its defect is 'specific to Example 1 and not a house convention' is half right: this pair does close and is a valid control, but Example 3 misses in the same direction and by more, so the deviation is not confined to Example 1. The three implied weights, 220.14, 217.39 and 227.27, are not one consistent wrong molecular weight either, so the pattern is imprecise mole figures rather than a single arithmetic error propagated. Example 3's pair belongs to Example 3's record and is flagged there or not there; it is recorded here only because Example 1's control claim rests on the comparison and a reader of this sidecar would otherwise inherit that claim uncorrected. NO MASS BALANCE TEST IS POSSIBLE: the patent prints 'Yield: 67%' but no isolated mass for NMSBA, so there is no printed mass to set against the printed input moles and no stated pair that disagrees; mass_balance_implausible is NOT raised. For the record and entering no field: 0.023 mol of NMSBA at 245.212 g/mol (C8H7NO6S, RDKit from CS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C(=O)O)c([N+](=O)[O-])c1) is 5.64 g theoretical, of which 67% is 3.78 g; neither number appears in the document. NOT MOLECULAR-WEIGHT CHECKABLE: sodium hypochlorite is charged as 100 ml with 0.149 mol, i.e. 1.49 M, the same concentration Example 1 implies from 500 ml and 0.745 mol, and concentrated hydrochloric acid as 18 mL with 0.17 mol, i.e. 9.44 M, which agrees with Example 3's 54 mL / 0.51 mol and differs from Example 1's 120 mL / 1.23 mol at 10.25 M. Both are solution volumes rather than masses of substance, so neither admits a molecular-weight check and neither was flagged; the acid molarity difference between Examples is recorded here because it is visible in the arithmetic, not because it is a defect. STOICHIOMETRY, computed but NOT written into the record because the patent states no equivalents: on the printed 0.023 mol of NMST, sodium hypochlorite is 6.48 eq, ruthenium oxide 0.174 eq and hydrochloric acid 7.39 eq. These are markedly higher than the 2.68, 0.040 and 4.42 eq the same figures give for Example 1, because the catalyst charge falls only from 1.5 g to 0.5 g while the substrate falls from 61.2 g to 5.0 g. That is what the patent prints; no scale_discontinuity flag applies, since that check compares a step to its own precursor and this step has none. SCALE: the limiting reagent charge is 5.0 g, so scale is lab (1 to 100 g). PURITY IS A MEASUREMENT REPORTED AS A BOUND, NOT A SPECIFICATION: the analytical line at 279 prints 'HPLC purity > 92%' for the single batch this Example made, so product_purity_pct is 92.0 with purity_method hplc, the inequality kept verbatim in quote_zh, procedure_text and the record notes, and 92.0 understood as that printed lower bound rather than an assayed equality. This agrees with A1, which holds purity_pct 92.0 and raw_text 'HPLC purity > 92%' for the same compound. It is 92% here against 95% in Examples 1 and 3, so the number is batch-specific and could not have been carried in from a neighbour. The summary section's 'at least 65%' and 'at least 85%' are specifications of the invention in general, are not measurements, and enter no numeric field of this record. 'Yield: 67%' is a measurement and is recorded; with no isolated mass printed it cannot be cross-checked.
